statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), operated by INPI, in coordination with the Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) held by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SAS statutes and corporate acts must be drawn up in French under the Code de commerce and the Toubon Law; the corporate name (dénomination sociale) may be in a foreign language only if transliterated into Latin alphabet characters; the name must be followed or preceded by the words 'Société par Actions Simplifiée' or the initials 'SAS' on all instruments and commercial documents, along with the company capital and registered office references.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank (reserved for authorized credit institutions)
Crédit / Établissement de crédit (reserved for ACPR-licensed credit institutions)
Établissement de monnaie électronique / Monnaie électronique (reserved for ACPR- or ECB-licensed electronic money institutions)
Assurance / Mutuelle (reserved for prudentially authorized insurance entities)
National / République / Prefecture / Ministère (official public authority indications)
Chambre de commerce / Bourse / Fonds de garantie (institutional or misleading claims)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Guichet unique rejects the proposed name on availability, trademark-conflict or regulatory-token grounds, the applicant may (i) submit a written administrative reconsideration within 10 working days through the Guichet unique dispute channel, attaching corrected evidence or an amended name; (ii) in the case of conflict with an existing RCS trade name or prior trademark, institute civil proceedings before the Tribunal judiciaire in the commercial formation in Paris seeking a declaration of non-deception or invalidity of the challenger's mark; (iii) in the case of rejection of a regulated-sector token, obtain the ACPR pre-authorization certificate or amend the name to remove the reserved term. Time limits for opposition follow the Intellectual Property Code (Article L711-3 et seq. and related transitional provisions).

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible: a SAS may be registered at an approved commercial domiciliation agency under Code de commerce Article L123-11-2, subject to a signed domiciliation contract and inclusion in the M0 filing; however, for an ACPR-licensed electronic money institution the ACPR requires effective management (direction effective), operational substance and a physical presence proportionate to the licensed activities on French territory, and a purely virtual office without local staff or systems will not satisfy the fit-and-proper or conduct-of-business requirements of the EMI licensing assessment.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very High: estimated 75% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 18 months after licensing, driven by the High_Risk_Special_License tier of the electronic money institution and the ACPR's scheduled on-site inspection program.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) through the official portal impots.gouv.fr; cross-border and large-taxpayer supervision by the Département des grandes entreprises and the Direction Nationale des Vérifications de Situations Fiscales. Customs and export controls are administered separately by the Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SAS is registered through the formalities portal (guichet unique). After the certificate of incorporation (Kbis) is issued, the local tax office (SIE) automatically allocates the SIREN and VAT identification number (FR + SIREN) without separate application. A non-established foreign entity carrying on a taxable supply in France must file the dedicated non-established taxable person registration form with the DGFIP office competent for non-resident taxpayers, provide proof of foreign incorporation, identification of a local tax representative when required, and state the date of commencement of French transactions. This VAT registration is mandatory before the first taxable transaction in France and is separate from the M0/Kbis incorporation procedure.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the SAS is a French-resident juridical person subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés) on worldwide profits; it is not a fiscally transparent entity. The entity has French territorial tax nexus for VAT, corporate income tax, social security and payroll taxes; no sub-jurisdictional tax distinction exists in France.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law does not use the check-the-box transparency election. Available elections are: (1) tax consolidation within a French group under article 223 A CGI where the parent holds at least 95% of the subsidiary; (2) the narrow option for income tax treatment under article 239 bis AB CGI available to small innovative or service SAS entities; (3) VAT optioning on equipment sale/lease under articles 260 CA/CB CGI; and (4) mandatory anti-hybrid mismatch and DAC6 disclosures through forms 2257-SD, 10023-SD and 3948-SD where the EMI participates in hybrid or paying-agent arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA – taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For French-established small taxable persons, the franchise in base de TVA exemption applies below €85,000 for goods and €37,500 for services. However, an electronic money institution (Établissement de Monnaie Électronique) and any non-French-established supplier are not covered by the franchise; VAT registration is required from the first taxable transaction even without turnover. Where the EMI only supplies VAT-exempt financial payment services under article 261 C CGI, registration may still be mandatory for statutory reporting, EU recapitulative statements and acquisition/import charging purposes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing under the 2023-2027 reform. Large and mid-size enterprises must issue e-invoices through certified dematerialisation platforms (PDP) or the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) from 1 September 2026; all businesses follow from 1 September 2027. Invoices must use Factur-X, UBL or CII formats and the transmission to the tax authority must occur through APIs conforming to the DGFIP digital interoperability standard. There is no central pre-approval stamping; instead the PPF performs post-transaction structured reporting, validation cross-checks, and invoice status acknowledgement. Each e-invoice must carry a guaranteed digital authenticity sideband including legal signature, audit trail and seamless re-integrity control.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported to a destination outside the European Union are zero-rated if the exporter proves that the goods physically left the EU. The proof consists of a validated customs export declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU) and the original transport documents. Intra-Community supplies to a business customer in another EU Member State are exempt from French VAT under article 262 ter CGI, subject to a valid French SIREN and the customer's EU VAT ID. Offshore business-to-business services to non-EU customers are treated as supplied where the customer is established and therefore fall outside the scope of French VAT, but the EMI must retain documentary evidence of customer location and business purpose. By contrast, electronic money issuance, payment accounts, transfers and the management of digital-wallet reserves are VAT-exempt under article 261 C 1° of CGI; they are not export zero-rated and carry only a pro-rata input VAT recovery right.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane / DAU) stamped or electronically validated by the DGDDI evidencing exit from the EU
Transport document proving physical export: Bill of Lading for sea freight, CMR or e-CMR for road freight, Air Waybill for air cargo, or shipped-in-bond document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement evidencing the foreign exchange repatriation into the French entity's bank account within the statutory period
Recapitulative statement of intra-Community sales for EU-destination goods and the customer's EU VAT identification number, where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export documentation must be preserved for at least six years. If zero-rating is applied without valid customs proof of export or without timely repatriation of the foreign sales proceeds, the French tax authority re-characterises the transaction as a domestic taxable sale and claws back the full 20% TVA plus interest at 5.00% per annum. The penalty regime under article 1788 A and 1731 CGI imposes 40% additional assessments for material inaccuracies, 80% for organised fraud, and criminal fines under article 1741 CGI for tax fraud; in cross-border export schemes the customs code also applies penalty duties of up to 100% of the value of the goods. Directors of the SAS may be held personally liable in cases of fraud or gross negligence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Central Bank and Eurosystem settlement authority), acting jointly with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution / French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority) and the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) as the statutory foreign exchange administration; the Banque de France is the competent central bank for TARGET2 settlement, domestic payment system oversight and balance-of-payments regulatory reporting, while the ACPR holds prudential and FX-risk supervision over licensed Electronic Money Institutions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full Eurozone member with unrestricted current-account and capital-account convertibility under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, OECD Capital Liberalisation Codes and the French Code Monétaire et Financier; the Euro is freely convertible and profit remittance is unrestricted provided that statutory distributable-reserve tests, corporate governance documentation and FATCA/CRS tax reporting requirements are satisfied; there are no prior exchange-control authorisations for non-resident equity investment into a French SAS; practical conversion hurdles are limited to AML-driven banking due diligence for large-size share premium receipts and the standard requirement that the capital be evidenced by a notarially-equivalent deed and entered into a dedicated bank account before the RCS corporate registry filing
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratio; the mandatory conversion ratio is 0% for Euro-denominated receipts and 0% for foreign-currency trade receivables which may be retained freely on external or domestic EEA accounts; this outcome is mandated by EU capital-movement liberalisation principles and the French General Tax Code reporting framework; only statistical balance-of-payments declaration duties apply to cross-border flows above the Banque de France reporting threshold (EUR 12,500), and no repatriation-maintenance period is imposed on export receivables

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Medium with legally constrained structuring; a licensed French EMI may use an offshore digital EMI only as a technical white-label distribution rail or as an agent, and cannot use a non-credit-institution as custodian of safeguarded funds because Article L521-3 of the French Code Monétaire et Financier requires that safeguarded funds be held with an EU/EEA-licensed credit institution; an EEA passporting EMI (Ireland or Lithuania) is legally admissible for processing SEPA flows but must be engaged under an outsourcing arrangement compliant with the EBA Outsourcing Guidelines, ACPR position 2020-03 and PSD2/EMD2 agency rules; a UK EMI is post-Brexit a third-country provider requiring licensed agent or branch structures and cannot be the primary Treasury bank; the recommended architecture is a tier-1 French bank for safeguarding and TARGET2 settlement, with an EEA EMI only for niche cross-border merchant-acquiring and faster-disbursement channels
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permitted in France through video-identification, certified eIDAS-qualified digital signatures and documentary verification under the ACPR Anti-Money-Laundering guidelines; in practice, tier-1 commercial banks impose an aggressive in-person counterparty due-diligence process for a High-Risk licensed EMI client whose scope includes virtual IBAN issuance; the de facto mandate is physical attendance at the bank's Paris corporate office by at least two executive directors, the Data Protection Officer, the AML Compliance Officer and the statutory representative of the principal UBO, including a live interview on the business plan, transaction monitoring architecture, sanction-screening engine and reserve-safeguarding method; if remote-only opening is attempted, a substantial negative outcome risk is underwriting refusal or a downgraded relationship tier, so the blueprint mandates one physical onboarding session before account activation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory status of the EMI and validity of the ACPR e-money license under verification by the onboarding bank
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the ACPR licence decision (agrément d'établissement de monnaie électronique), the final statutory articles of association explicitly limiting activities to e-money issuance, distribution and redemption, operational programme filed with ACPR, safeguarding funds attestation from the prior commercial partner, proof of initial capital / own funds in the licensed amount, and the latest ACPR regulatory correspondence confirming no corrective measures

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unidentified ultimate beneficial owners outside the EEA and unwinding of opaque SPV chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (UBO register) excerpt, notarised corporate chain chart from the French entity to the final natural-person shareholders, certificated share transfer deeds, audited financial statements for each intermediate holding entity, tax residence certificates, passports and source-of-wealth declarations, and a signed group-structure letter produced by a Paris-based law firm

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business model involving virtual IBAN issuance and digital wallet reserve management triggering enhanced due diligence under Article L561-10 of the French AML Code
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group-wide AML/CTF policy aligned with the 5AMLD/6AMLD, transaction-monitoring system description (screenings, thresholds, AI suspicions), customer look-through KYC program for all virtual IBAN end-users, independent annual AML audit report, a sanctions-screening confirmation covering EU, UN, OFAC and French FIC/AMF lists, and the designated AML Compliance Officer's professional due-diligence record in French banking compliance

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection source-of-funds and potential undisclosed financing by third-party funds recyclers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT103 credit confirmation evidencing originator identity, parent company signed declaration of the lawful provenance of the subscribed funds, intermediate bank reference letters, audited statutory accounts of the subscribing shareholder, third-party forensic Enhanced Due Diligence report, notarised share-subscription minutes, and confirmation that the injection route was a direct credit from an EEA bank account of the immediate parent to the SAS account

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: subscriber transfers the official EUR share capital into the dedicated capital-escrow account of the French SAS at the onboarding tier-1 bank using a SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA originators or an ISO 20022 SEPA Credit Transfer for EEA originators; for SEPA purposes the Purpose Code 'INTC' (intra-group transfer) is used, and the remittance information field carries the French descriptor 'Apport de Capital' together with the Banque de France balance-of-payments direct-investment classification code 'Participation/Investissement Direct'; the bank's compliance desk must receive pre-funding the investment file consisting of the certified board resolution, the shareholder subscription deed, approval of UBOs, source-of-funds statements, tax-residence certificates and the bank's own sanctions screening release prior to credit; post-credit, the capital-attestation certificate and the notarised articles with paid-in capital are executed for the RCS registration
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement rails: EUR-denominated payouts across the Eurozone and for EEA counterparties clear via TARGET2 (Banque de France participation of the commercial bank) using SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) up to the EUR 100,000 limit; high-value treasury operations and non-EEA trade settlements in USD, GBP, CHF, or CNY execute over the SWIFT network using MT103 Single Customer Credit Transfer and MT202 COV cover payments; for physical imported goods requiring customs-oriented documentary evidence, Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 are advised and financed by the tier-1 bank's trade-finance department, and for high-risk suppliers a Confirmed Irrevocable LC is used to retain control on title documents and bill of lading release conditions
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable forward contracts with ISDA/SUPRA master agreement
EUR/GBP deliverable forward contracts for UK trade disbursements
EUR/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for China-payable obligations where onshore CNY deliverability is restricted
EUR/INR non-deliverable forwards (NDF) for Indian supplier settlements in non-fully-convertible INR
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps between EUR and USD matching the expected revenue recognition cycles and safeguarding-asset yields
FX options and collar structures for hedging contingent cash flows in merchant payout portfolios
EUR/CHF deliverable forwards for Swiss franc treasury inflows and distribution of group dividends

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements (comptes annuels) and management report, as approved by shareholders, filed at the commercial register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder decision within 6 months of fiscal year end; registry filing within 1 month after approval, therefore no later than 7 months after fiscal year end; period extendable by court order upon justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of EUR 1,500 plus EUR 15 per day; possible additional penalty of EUR 20,000 for false or omitted information; administrative strike-off proceeding may be opened after 3 months of uninterrupted failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liassez fiscale, including form n°2065 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months of fiscal year end; for fiscal year ending 31 December, extension operates to the second business day immediately following 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment penalty of 5% of assessed tax plus delay interest of 0.20% per month; formal notice assessment may add 40% penalty; possible prosecution for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO declaration and confirmation of beneficial owners (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs), updated and presented with the annual accounts filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (RCS) through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial declaration within 30 days of registration; any modification, including share transfers changing ownership or control, within 30 days; annual confirmatory update lodged at the same time as the annual accounts if a change occurred during the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine up to EUR 15,000 for the legal representative and, in cases of intentional concealment, imprisonment up to 6 months and fine up to EUR 375,000 at corporate level; administrative sanctions including denial of registry extracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual regulatory and prudential reporting to the financial supervisor, including annual qualitative report and statutory financial data under ACPR instructions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) / Banque de France
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year end or on the exact date set in the ACPR supervisory correspondence; quarterly REM and reporting data submitted separately under the ACPR reporting calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential disciplinary warning, monetary penalty imposed by the ACPR Enforcement Committee, restriction of electronic-money issuance activity, and ultimately withdrawal of the electronic-money institution licence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory if at the end of the financial year the company exceeds two of the three French thresholds: balance sheet total EUR 4,000,000, turnover excluding VAT EUR 8,000,000, and average permanent staff 50. In all cases, a licensed electronic-money institution is subject to perpetual ACPR-required independent audit and control because of its special licence, regardless of whether the size thresholds are met.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory individual accounts under French local GAAP, applying the Plan Comptable Général and the French Commercial Code articles L.123-12 et seq.; consolidated or combined IFRS financial statements may be prepared under EU-adopted IFRS when applicable. The licensed EMI must also comply with ACPR accounting and financial reporting instructions implementing the EBA/EMI framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The register of beneficial owners must be lodged with the RCS and kept at the registered office. Any transfer of shares, change in control, or variation in the natural-person beneficial ownership must be declared to the registry within 30 days. Where no change occurs, the existing declaration remains valid; the annual accounts filing procedure includes confirmation that the UBO information is current, and a corrected declaration is submitted immediately if an inaccuracy is identified.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 220 - 650 per year for licensed registered-office or business domiciliation services in France; high-end range applies for regulated-entity premises and correspondence-handling provisions.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 30,000 - 85,000 per year for an independent certified audit (commissariat aux comptes) of a licensed French electronic-money institution with virtual IBAN and digital-wallet activities, depending on transaction volume, number of subsidiaries, and group audit scope.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (deduction up to 100% of eligible R&D expenses); innovation tax credit; standard 25% rate applies to electronic money institutions with no sector-specific holidays

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form IS 1201 - Déclaration de résultat (electronic filing via impots.gouv.fr)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., May 15 for calendar year)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Résultat fiscal avant application des régimes particuliers
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or loss before special regimes and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only French-source income; claim WHT credits on repatriated amounts
Apply R&D credits and other incentives; non-residents limited to French-source items

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 0.5% of turnover per month (maximum 25% of turnover); non-filing: 40% penalty; interest at 0.2% per month on unpaid tax

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% standard rate; reduced under bilateral treaties (0-15%)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain TRC (Tax Residency Certificate) from French tax authorities; submit claim form and supporting documentation via impots.gouv.fr or bilateral treaty procedures
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% under most treaties; Interest: 0% under OECD model treaties (France generally applies 0% WHT on interest to non-residents)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50 million EUR annual turnover for local file; 750 million EUR for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France implements DAC6 reporting for economic substance in IP holding and certain activities; EMI licensing requires operational substance in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to file corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of IS 1201 declaration by deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 0.5% of turnover per month late (max 25% of turnover); 40% flat penalty for non-filing; possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors jointly liable for tax debts; possible imprisonment for fraudulent behavior; civil restitution orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length prices or failing to prepare TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments up to 500% of understated tax; penalties up to 500% of additional tax; criminal sanctions in severe cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for tax shortfalls; possible disqualification from management; imprisonment for willful misconduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold and remit WHT on dividends, royalties, or interest to non-residents
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 10% of unpaid WHT; interest on delayed payments; possible criminal evasion charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for withheld amounts; potential jail time for intentional evasion; fines

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Economic substance violation or shell company abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining French entity without sufficient economic activity or for tax avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of transactions; denial of deductions; penalties up to 500% of tax benefit; criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors liable for restitution; possible prison sentences for fraudulent schemes
